findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk error).
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use ? or map_err to propagate the error.

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing on a Vec with no bounds validation before access.
findings.failure_mode: A line with zero commas produces a single-element Vec; indexing [0] is safe but any future reordering or logic change that accesses beyond the actual length will panic.
findings.fix: Use parts.get(0) with if-let or match to handle the missing-field case explicitly.

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing without verifying the Vec has at least 2 elements.
findings.failure_mode: A line missing a comma or trailing field yields a 1-element Vec; parts[1] panics at runtime with index-out-of-bounds.
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1) with if-let or match to handle the missing-field case, or restructure with split_once to guarantee the two-field contract.

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16. Values > 65535 silently truncate.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value like 70000 becomes 4369 in u16, silently corrupting data with no error indication.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) or parse::<u16>() directly, returning a typed parse/overflow error.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric or out-of-range input in the value field.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data (e.g., 'bad_value') aborts the entire batch load instead of skipping or reporting the offending record.
findings.fix: Use parse::<u16>() with ? or map_err, combining parse failure and overflow into a single typed error.

findings.problem: println!() call inside the map closure introduces a hidden I/O side effect in a function that should be a pure core or at least not mix logging into data transformation.
findings.failure_mode: Debug logging cannot be conditionally disabled; output order is nondeterministic with iterators; side effects are hidden inside a closure that the caller does not expect.
findings.fix: Remove println! from the core. If logging is required, push it to the imperative shell boundary and return data-only records from the core function.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> to extract two fields, when split_once would suffice.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation and string cloning per line degrades performance, especially for large files.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to split into exactly two &str parts, then trim and parse each side without intermediate Vec allocation.

findings.problem: load_batchs returns Vec<Record> with no error type. All failures (I/O, parse, indexing, overflow) are silent panics.
findings.failure_mode: The caller has no way to distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from integer overflow; there is no error taxonomy.
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum (e.g., LoadError { Io(io::Error), Parse(String), Overflow { field: String, value: String } }) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>.

findings.problem: Record has pub fields with no validation invariants; name can be any string, value can be any u16 including 0 if that is invalid.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct invalid Records (e.g., empty name, negative-as-u16) without the domain enforcing its own invariants.
findings.fix: Make fields private, provide a constructor that validates invariants, or use a newtype for name (e.g., NonEmptyString).

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for batch loading performance
no profiler data for allocation profile of load_batchs
no allocation tracking or second-ring evidence for Vec/String allocations per record
no command-line interface or executable entry point evidence (binary target missing from Cargo.toml)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has 5 BLOCKER violations (unwrap on I/O, unwrap on parse, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, hidden side-effect logging), 3 WARNINGs (split_once misuse, no error type, no invariants), and 4 missing evidence items. All BLOCKERs cause panics or data corruption on realistic inputs. The function must be rewritten to return Result with typed errors, use split_once, eliminate all unwrap/as, remove println!, and validate invariants before this crate can be considered compliant.
